<meta>The previous page concluded a series of specific physiological observations regarding vision (double vision in the intoxicated) and animal biology (the sleeping habits of hares and the properties of fluids in colts). This page transitions into a more theoretical and philosophical discussion on the nature of "Nature" (Physis) itself, focusing on its generative powers, its relationship to matter, and how it ensures that offspring resemble their parents.</meta>

The master of things of the same kind, then, is both first by nature and is so named, since the term "alike" is understood through both reason and common belief. Let it be called, for me, both the act of drinking and <unclear>fillings</unclear> <note>likely referring to the replenishment of bodily fluids or humors</note>, and whatever other things might come to those who seek. The path that is seen, observed without passion, is worthy to be, and is a fifth thing, from which the distance has been made.

For the power that bears itself from impulse rejoices in its own form, moving and conversing with itself most of all; it is a guarantee and a perfect starting point to use and a defined release. Nature, therefore, is what underlies this. In this same way—by Zeus—whether through power or the principle of being moved, it is named Nature. From this, Nature receives its name: for she is herself born and makes things grow, already representing the all-working power in nature. Within her is the material mass; she is the one who kindles this together with nature, or something upon nature. For from what occurs, she gave power to matter, just as I already said she formed it. Nature is the one who adds to this; therefore, all things are brought down from her, and she alone moves the earth, even if she herself completes the excellence through all things without succession. For at that time, <term>breath</term> <note>original: pneuma; the vital spirit or "wind" that animates the body</note> came forth, rolling over the place.

When <term>Nature</term> <note>original: physis</note> approached, she brought three powers: <term>generative</term> <note>original: gennetika; the ability to reproduce</note>, <term>nutritive</term> <note>original: threptika; the ability to sustain life through food</note>, and <term>growth-oriented</term> <note>original: auxetika; the ability to increase in size</note>. There is matter and a guarantee for the body; she gave the ability to move through time, and the power of nutrition is the best. In every way, the powers of nature are arranged here. She bestows the dignity of virtue, whether through growth or generation, or things entirely similar. It is now clear that these have been joined, and this is shown in truth, as some speak more extensively about the leadership in the preservation of living beings. 

Hence, the <term>material</term> <note>original: hylike</note> power is already a fermentation of the flesh. In males, there is a pulse of impulse toward the likeness of birth, wanting to project a form not toward others, but most of all toward the sight, which occurs because of this likeness in nature. In this, they happen upon knowledge, making faith for themselves; she brings her own material imprint to her own mind.

<column-break/>

The child becomes like the parent, or however it happens toward us; for they possess a persistence regarding the state of the senses and preserve the mastery of it.

# + The Book of Dream Interpretation which was composed and arranged
## by Achmet, son of Seirim, the dream interpreter of the Chief Counselor 
## Mamun <note>original: "Mamemeu," likely referring to the Abbasid Caliph al-Ma'mun, who reigned from 813 to 833 AD</note> :-

<margin><unclear>Note:</unclear></margin>
-> Prologue : <-

Often and in every <unclear>way</unclear>, I have received from my masters the precise <margin><unclear>...</unclear></margin> interpretation of dreams, just as I held them in my memory; in the ancient manner of the poets, they were called to such precision. Therefore, out of affection and the benefit of faith—to which an infinite multitude incline—I have remembered and considered it right to create this exposition for the entirety of the present interpretation. **I**f someone sees that he is eating the head of a sheep, he will find great joy and wealth. If he sees that he ate the head of another, the rich man will act maliciously toward a superior head [authority], and perhaps he will even be disciplined by his God. 

If he sees that he was seeking a head for himself from a stag—or wearing the head of irrational animals—he will be considered like a beast. Such a person takes on a great office. If the animal's size indicates a small bodily office, he will be favored. Anything strange or monstrous in a vision is significant, except for the stag and that which is auspicious. If someone sees a colt, he must keep watch over these things, for as for his humanity, he will find friendship, for this is what he must find.

For if someone sees that his hair has spread out—if someone sees even the hairs on his body, that he has adorned and multiplied them—not only will they increase, but so will the ornament of the wealth of his house. If he sees that the hairs of his beard have died in a wandering fashion <note>The text here is difficult; "wandering" (πολυπλανῶς) likely refers to a tangled or unkempt beard.</note>, he will grow rich and flourish. But if he sees these hairs bare, or plucked out as if cast aside, it refers to his daughters or his benefactor. If someone sees that his hairs were about to fall asleep <note>Likely a metaphor for falling out or losing vitality.</note> and become fewer, he will be punished carelessly or cast off in the matter of the royal [court]. 

If he sees that the hairs of his neck have been untangled, the old man is freed from grief and fear, though he may need a trembling slave nearby. If someone sees the hairs of his body are white and dry, he may hope for joy. 

If a woman sees these things: if they have multiplied, she will suffer certain afflictions and be punished by them. But if they were cast off, she will find joy through marriage. If she is unmarried, she will lose her virginity. Regarding the feet and the wings <note>original: "πτερῶν" — can mean feathers or fins, but in this context, it may refer to the extremities or metaphorical 'wings' of the soul/status.</note>: however much the hairs of the beard multiply, they bring joy. If he is poor, he will find wealth and reach the fringes of it. If he sees that the hairs of his armpits have multiplied so that they descend to his sides, he will find wealth.

If someone sees in a dream that he speaks with another and his voice is short and weak, he will find benefit; generally, his soul will be adorned. ### Concerning eyelids and eyebrows: they are the ornament of the eyes, according to the physicians

The eyelids and the eyebrows are the ornament <note>original: κόσμος (kosmos); this term implies both beauty and the orderly arrangement of the face.</note> of the eyes. For if you see that your eyelids and eyebrows are opened wide, you shall be pleasing in your faith <note>original: πίστις (pistis); in Byzantine dream-books, this refers both to religious devotion and one's reputation for reliability.</note> and you shall rejoice in your children. But if you see them tightly bound, if it be for a king, he shall become an exile and face fear of his enemies, and he shall not prevail. If he be of the common people, he shall reach old age with glory, and he shall not lose his faith. If someone sees his eyebrows shaved and rotting, he will not have the same pride in the honoring of his children, nor shall he have glory regarding his sons. If someone sees that his eyebrows fell out as if he were a leper <note>original: λελωβημένου; refers to one suffering from a mutilating disease or leprosy.</note>, if he be a king, his affairs shall perish and his army will be poorly managed. For the common people, God will not look upon him with favor, and his possessions will be diminished from among all his goods.

The eyebrows and eyelids are the glory of the face. If they are worthy—meaning they were previously increased and adorned—he will find glory and honor after a period of sorrow, and an old age spent against his enemies. And if there is a pending marriage, he will be joined to the woman he desires and will grow rich. If someone sees that these were muzzled <note>original: ἐφημώθησαν; likely meaning the eyes were forced shut or the hair was stripped away.</note> and fell out, if he be a king, his children shall inherit his kingdom and devour it; it shall be snatched from him. And in the midst of his spouse, enmity and hatred shall be cut off. For the common people, whatever property and ornament they have set aside, they shall lose it...

### The forehead and the temple

These are the ornament and wealth in the midst of the ages <note>original: αἰώνων (aionon); in this context, it likely refers to the dreamer's generation or the public sphere.</note>. If, therefore, someone sees in a dream that his forehead was widened and more adorned,

he will find power and wealth in the midst of his generation. But if he sees that it was humbled or sunken, it signifies old age spent against his enemies. And though there may be a stumbling in his faith, there shall be a broadening of his soul. If someone sees that his forehead was enlarged on both sides of his face, he will be deceived and shall be put to shame before the public. Even if [he is] of the Persians, and according to faith he sees the forehead, the barrier of the future arrives. But if someone sees that his forehead was broken or suffered injury, he will be stripped of his wealth and will live in fear and trembling. <meta>This page continues the systematic interpretation of facial features in dreams, moving from the eyes and forehead to the mouth, teeth, and tongue. It maintains the characteristic Byzantine "Oneirocriticon" style, which distinguishes between the prophetic meaning of a dream for a king or ruler versus a common citizen or a poor man.</meta>

If someone sees that his teeth were injured from blows, this suffering <note>original: πάθος (pathos); implies both an injury and the emotional suffering resulting from it.</note> refers to his children and the downfall of his house. But if he sees that one of the teeth falls out and comes to the guardian of his house, his lineage [is affected] in regard to his wife. If he sees this before eating and drinking: if someone sees that with boldness and gaping wide—and his mouth is widened in an orderly way—if he be a king or a lord of a people, he shall have boasts and glories from war. But if he be of the common people, he shall have boasts and glories in his affairs, and the beauty of his soul shall increase. 

If he sees that he sent something away from the parts of the mouth, or from the aforementioned place; if he sees his mouth filled with flesh in front of the people or many: if he be a king, it signifies that there is a treasure in his house, most beautiful, and a reduction of his court <note>original: προσώπων (prosopon); literally "faces," but in a court context refers to the people surrounding the king.</note>. But if he be of the common people, it signifies poverty. 

If someone sees that his mouth was heated <note>original: ἐτέφθη; likely a corruption of a word for burning or heating.</note> according to the excess of its power, then every good thing will come to an end, either from the women or from his beloved ones.

<margin>20</margin> Concerning the teeth of a man: they are all judged according to his relatives. Those in the front correspond to legitimate children or brothers and sisters. And if one tooth is more distinguished than the others, it represents a distinction among the relatives. If, therefore, someone sees one of those front teeth becoming a back tooth, or it turned black, or became worm-eaten <note>original: ἐσκωληκίασεν; a common term for dental decay, comparing the cavity to a worm-hole.</note>, he shall have trouble for one of the prominent members of the lineage. 

But if someone sees those same teeth whiter and more favorable, he shall find joy and beauty for the descendants of the lineage. If he sees that one of the teeth is longer than another, he shall receive indignation and affliction from those specific relatives. If he sees that another tooth grew out with them, separated from the others,

<column-break/>

then that person—whether a child, a possession, or a brother—was made desolate and wiped out from the others of the lineage; it signifies poverty and everything related to the poor. 

But if he sees that his tooth fell and was overshadowed by his tongue, or the tongue was enlarged so that he was unable to turn it, the people shall be carefree, but in his judgments he shall stumble; he shall be deaf, he shall be dulled, and he shall lose his wisdom. In the manner of enemies, it shall oppose him, and he shall be greatly afflicted. If this dream be for the common people, he will be either poor or [struggle] in his ways of life. Because he shall find things to relate without ceasing having seen this, he shall find joy and desire in his possessions. For through the tongue, a man is made certain of his affairs. 

If someone sees that his tongue appeared leprous and thick, if he be a king, all things shall be ordered by his judgments, and he shall be wondrous and pure. If he be of the common people, he shall win his lawsuit without worry, and in his affairs, he shall be guided well. 

But if he sees a fall <note>original: πτῶμα; can also mean a corpse or a ruin.</note>—not from hatred or shame from his wife—directed at some of the courtly persons and from pains; if someone sees his tongue, that it became mute <note>original: ἄλαλος (alalos); literally "without speech."</note>: if he be a king, the chief of his scribes <note>original: ὑπογραφέων; can refer to secretaries, legal scriveners, or those who sign on his behalf.</note> will be in danger, and he himself will be afflicted in his cares for his beloved ones. 

If such a dream is for a common person, the place will be troubled, and the bitterness of his heart shall not be made manifest. If he be poor, his affairs will be despaired of; he goes out of life, he shall be in shame and treated as refuse <note>original: σκυβαλισμῷ; from 'skybalon' meaning dung or rubbish.</note> before the face of men. 

If someone sees that his beauty is comely, if he be a king, he shall distribute justice to his son or grant him a release, and give glory to him.

If someone sees that one of the thick teeth fell out or turned black, and he mourns, one of his relatives in their prime will fall ill. # The Interpretation of Dreams

If he experiences many things, he will be industrious <note>original: φιλερπὴς (philerpēs), literally "fond of moving or striving," suggesting a diligent person</note> in all things and will prosper according to that experience. If he dreams that he is hungry and receives satiation, the worry and mourning for himself and his house will cease, just as he finds satisfaction in the dream. If he dreams that he was kissed by one of his own relatives: if it is by his father and it is frequent and easy, his life will be light and easy, and much gold shall be added to him. But if the kiss is not <note>The Greek "thalo" is obscure here, perhaps meaning "flourishing"</note> flourishing and full, but rather harsh, it will end in affliction, bitterness, and worldly trouble. This is the interpretation regarding the limbs and these matters.

If he dreams that his belly has come forward and grown large, his house and his wealth will increase. However, some ancient sages <note>A reference to the long tradition of "Oneirocriticon" or dream-interpretation manuals from antiquity</note> used to say that if it was filled but then contracted, it lightens one’s worries and indicates a house full of the joy of wealth. If someone sees that they are squeezing or constricting him around the belly, he will find affliction and worry within his house. If he dreams of an outpouring from his belly as if from a wound requiring treatment, he has lost his household <note>original: φαμιλίαν (phamilian), a Greek transliteration of the Latin "familia," referring to the domestic staff and family</note> quickly and truly.

<margin>Regarding the breasts and shoulders from the works of Daniel and the others</margin>
**The breasts** undoubtedly allow for distinction: if someone sees his breasts or nipples as healthy and fat, he will find joy in his daughter. If someone sees that he was wounded or struck there, disease will come upon his daughters; or if he has no daughters, his old age will be weaker, and the suffering will fall upon the females of his house.

<margin>From the same sources</margin>
**The shoulder blades** refer to the status of the wives and the man’s own core—or perhaps the children before him. If someone sees his shoulder blade thrust out or taken away, it will be a test of the status of his wives, and any occurring battle will be clarified. But if he sees that they have grown large and thick with strength, his wife will gain glory, wealth, and good things.

<column-break/>

...his ship, as if it were undervalued. But if he sees that the shoulder blade was dislocated from him, he will soon be separated from his wife by her death. If he sees this part of the body naked, and if he has a daughter, she will pass away. Elsewhere it is written: a relative or an old friendship will come to an end. The shoulder blades signify either these people or his wealth and strength. Therefore, when their arms are weakened <note>original: ἀπικωρηνται (apikōrēntai), a likely corruption of a word meaning to be exhausted or withdrawn</note>, if he dreams that the liver <term>ἧπαρ (hēpar): the liver was considered the seat of life and the source of blood</term> is in his shoulder blade, they are weighed down by the burden of it. From his own burden, the affliction passes to others—to the nephews or the grandchildren. Likewise, if he sees that his shoulder blades became strong, large, and broad, he will be famous, as will the sons who come after him.

<margin>From the works of Daniel</margin>
**Take heart** <note>The text uses "Tharrei" (Be bold) as a section marker or encouraging note</note> if he dreams that his entrails came out through the anus and hung down: the household will depart from his house together with his possessions, but they will return again, provided the entrails were not completely cut off. But by this very sight, he will also be afflicted. If he dreams that he ate from his own entrails, he will find wealth from his own labors. Likewise, if he sees that he ate the entrails of another, he will grow wealthy from others. If he dreams that his liver was cast out from the anus, his treasure will be uncovered, but he himself will die. For the liver is the "root of the blood," and blood signifies gold and wealth. The breath of the spirit <note>original: πνοὴ τοῦ πνεύματος (pnoē tou pneumatos), likely referring to a divine or prophetic wind</note> will convince the people; a bitter disease will be cured and he will be restored, and in this manner, he will eventually die. If he dreams that fire from another was found and he ate it, he will find a treasure proportional to the fear of the danger he faced. These things are distinguished in like manner.

# On the Outcome of Poverty
If a rich man sees [this], he has lost his wealth. And it will appear to those same people. He will exist in poverty. But if a poor man [sees it], he will grow <note>The Greek "γέσω" is likely a corruption of "γηράσω" (grow old).</note> and end his life in poverty. If a woman sees this, she will be filled <note>original: μεστηθήσεται (mestēthēsetai); likely meaning becoming "full" or pregnant.</note> by her husband. She will acquire possessions. If someone sees in a dream that he was **crucified** <note>In Byzantine dream interpretation, crucifixion is often a positive sign of "elevation" in status for the poor, though a sign of public exposure or ruin for the rich.</note> while wearing **white garments**, he will have moved well and will relocate to another place. Regarding poverty, he will be provided for. And he will rejoice greatly in his spouse. If someone sees that his **ribs** <note>original: πλευρὰς (pleuras)</note> on the right side have changed color, he will face a burning long-term illness in his side. If someone sees in a dream that his ribs or his **flesh** did [something], he will find a way to distribute many **gold coins** <term>nomisma: the standard gold currency of the Byzantine Empire</term>. And he will find honor from his protective amulets... <note>The text here is fragmented.</note> doing harm. Out of his affairs. If someone sees in a dream that by a judgment he was **hanged** by necessity, he will be honored with a good dignity <note>A "dignity" refers to an official title or rank in the imperial court.</note> of that place where he hung. But the giving of these things does not cause harm. These things will be cast away. And at the end, he will prevail. Likewise, if someone says he received a foundation for himself, he will be blessed... he will be angered and enraged at the matter and will be humbled. And later, he [the superior] will honor him. But the one who is honored will act impiously and sin. If someone sees in a dream that his flesh or ribs were dried up... because of his sins... accordingly as he ate. ...from the faithful and the wealthy.

If someone sees in a dream that he was **crucified**, if he is poor, he will become rich. But if he is rich, it signifies punishment. He will inherit a counterfeit wealth. If someone sees in a dream that he was **flogged** <note>original: εδάφην (edaphēn); likely referring to being beaten with an ox-hide whip.</note> and then crucified, regarding the beating: he will have authority over the people and will be patient in all things. If someone sees in a dream that he was crucified and **descended from the height**, he will fall from his dignity and his wealth will be taken away.

<column-break/>

If someone sees in a dream that he was crucified and **bought**, he will be subject to and yet rule over people. And after these things, by the necessity of war, he will be destroyed by fire... from the springs. 

The **ribs** represent the stars of his **wife**. The upper and middle ribs are his wife herself. The lower ribs are other female relatives. If someone sees in a dream that his **upper ribs were broken**, the suffering will come to him from his wife, or her family, or her portion. But if he sees that the **lower ribs were broken**, he will be distressed by the female members of his kindred. If someone sees in a dream that his ribs became **strong and wide**, he will find joy in his wife, or in the power of his household. The ribs are the **walls of the house**. The ribs also represent the guardians of the house who are made bright. For whether they do well or do ill, it shows in the face of those guardians. 

If someone sees in a dream that certain first ribs were broken, the **steward** <term>oikonomos: the manager of the household assets</term> of the house will die. And he himself will be distressed afterward. If someone sees in a dream that his ribs were surrounded and grew, his wealth will be secure. And the guardians will find joy. 

Regarding the **hips** <note>original: ἰσχία (ischia)</note>, the **kidneys**, and the **sinews**: The hips judge regarding the person who sees them. All his power is shown there. If someone sees in a dream that his hips were **enlarged** or widened and grew strongly, he will find strength in himself according to his years and he will grow rich. If someone sees in a dream that his **hips were broken** in part, or through disease he is unable to walk, he will enter into distress and will have **childlessness** <note>original: ἀτεκνίαν (ateknian)</note>. If someone sees in a dream that he was poisoned or suffered in the hips, he will die quickly; this applies similarly to both the poor and the rich. If someone sees in a dream that his hips <unclear>failed</unclear> or turned... he will find joy in a woman.

<meta>This page continues the manual’s systematic guide to body parts in dreams, moving from the torso and "demonic possession" of the previous page to the lower extremities—the feet and legs. In the symbolic language of this text, the feet represent the "support" of a person's life: their servants, their wealth, and their physical lifespan. As is typical for this genre, the meaning of a dream changes depending on whether the dreamer is a king, a commoner, or a poor person.</meta>

If she <gloss>the foot</gloss> was kicked and cut off behind him, <note>original: ελακτισθη (elaktisthē); refers to a violent strike or kick</note> if he is of the elite, he is separated from his primary and secret office. But if he is of the common people, he will lose half of the essence <note>original: πνευμα (pneuma); literally "spirit," here meaning the core or vital part</note> of his wealth. And if he asks about it, he will be deprived of what he has claimed. But if he is poor, he will lose the defense of his servants’ cause. If anyone sees that his two feet were cut off, if he is a king, he will be short-lived; and before his death, he shall lose both his household and his faithful followers. If he is of the common people, swift poverty and punishment will overtake them. If he is poor, he will bury that which he holds dear and will himself soon be buried.

If anyone sees that his legs became iron, he shall be made powerful or shall endure; it signifies long life and that he shall trample his enemies. As for the wicked place of his servants, he shall be greatly glorified. If he is of the common people, he shall find wealth as great as that of the powerful, and a good life. If it is a woman, she shall rejoice in the things she desires and shall be called blessed.

If anyone sees that his legs became glass <note>original: υέλου (hyelou); glass was a symbol of fragility</note>, he shall be short-lived; and he shall sail recklessly through the fragile glass. ### Omens of Children and Adultery

with the gold, he shall suffer pain alongside peace and grace, and later on, because of the stone and the **pearl**. 

If he sees that he placed **rings** around her, he shall desire a certain longing; both of them shall be [placed]. But if he sees that he lost the setting of her seal-ring, he shall find joy quickly. If he sees it was cast into water, he shall be joined in marriage. If he sees that she lost her ring, she shall lose her wealth and die in poverty. If he sees that she lost her **bracelet** <note>original: βραχίονα (brachiona); literally "arm," but contextually referring to the arm-ring or bracelet mentioned previously</note>, she shall be abandoned due to distress.

### Clothing and Childbirth

But if he sees his wife in **red garments**, they shall find joy and bear a male child. If she wears white or perhaps yellow garments—without shoes—he shall be negligent, but she shall bear a male child. However, regarding **men’s shoes**, they signify an incursion and distress in all his works, as well as a painful fight, turmoil, and division. 

If he sees that his husband first gave her a **naked** state <note>This refers to the wife appearing naked in the dream</note>:
*   If she is pregnant, she shall bear a female child.
*   If she is not, she shall conceive and bear a female child.
*   If she has no husband, she has been enslaved to some and shall be in his joy.

If he sees that her garment was stolen, her daughter or her slave-girl shall fall ill. If other things were stolen, he shall be grieved over <margin>sa</margin> his daughter and the female servant, or regarding a marriage among the younger ones.

### Celebrations and Music

If he sees that he prepared a **wedding banquet**, he will be helped by the thanks of his authority. If he sees himself playing with them, he brings a loss of substance upon himself. If **cymbals** <note>original: κύμβαλα (kymbala)</note> clattered at the doors and those playing them were pleasing, it shall bring hope and wailing. 

If someone sees that he strikes an instrument or sings while hanging, or sings a "breath" <note>original: πνοην (pnoen); perhaps a specific type of melodic sigh or spiritual song</note>, he shall find others and give of himself to others. But if he sees that the songs turn into waters at the springs, he shall be long-lived; and his authority and the source of the voice of his songs shall be inscribed.

If someone sees that a person dead for a long time has risen and says, "I did not die, but I live," as he testifies by being seen, the salvation of the dead man is judged; it is a full assurance of the divine proof <note>original: θεογραφελέγχ (theographelench); an abbreviated form likely meaning "divine testimony" or "scriptural proof"</note> that he did not even perish. From the same source: If anyone sees a **circle**, he is deceived by his own experience and shall not bring his task to completion. If one sees a leather strap cleaning away filth, [this signifies] sorrow from the punishment of a ruler. But if from the feet and [unclear] <margin>9</margin> if one believes he takes a **purgative** <note>original: κάθαρσιον (katharsion); a medicinal treatment used to "cleanse" the body, often used as a metaphor for spiritual or financial purging</note> and is benefited, his possessions shall be lost as a penalty. But if he sells a snare, he shall receive some benefit from his children.

If a woman sees that she has been purged, the child in her womb shall perish, and she shall not bear another. But if this happens to a stranger, or if her craft is penalized, she shall handle good things with joy and acquire worldly possessions. If one believes that he is being cleansed and a great, unclean multitude departs from the city, this person shall become exceedingly poor and be pelted with stones. 

If one believes he takes a visible and clear medicine and clearly sees the things within his body through his own watchfulness, then the affairs of his enemies shall be punished. But if someone sees that he receives medicine from someone and it remains within them all, another person shall become poor through a lack of resources. But if it is done in haste, he shall destroy the deceit of his enemies. 

If one sees that he takes medicine and experiences a vision, he shall acquire wealth in part from whatever ruler is in power; but these are his own [possessions]. If someone sees that he takes medicine and it affects his eyes, and they become exceedingly scaly <note>original: ἐλεπώθη (elepōthē); likely referring to a condition like leprosy or scaling, symbolizing a loss of clarity or social standing</note>, he shall find a name and honor from the authorities, but in various places he shall face insult and become weak. If one sees that he takes a pit <note>this appears to be a corruption in the text, perhaps meaning "takes a draught from a pit"</note> as a medicine and drinks it visibly, he is redeemed from his necessity, or rather, from death.

If one believes in a dream that he is marking out his own **boundary of lands**, he shall find himself in a state of good order and truth. But if one does not wish for the boundary—

<column-break/>

—but it is long and without exit, he shall find wealth proportional to the joy, and also to his own boundary. If anyone considers his abundance and the world of his partial intellect: if he sees a country or one that has valleys and plains, his health and wealth are distinguished by this. If it is a land of wheat or of toilsome labors, the distinction of money shall be cut short through care and toil. And if it is passed through by fire and other things toward the irrigated part of the mountain, it is distinguished by affliction and punishment.

But if there is wheat along with wax, these things distinguish wealth that comes through exchange, along with very many joys. If it is the unpaved floor of a house, it signifies the opening of wealth and good management. If someone recognizes these things from his labors and retreats, it distinguishes abundance in these matters. If anyone receives from a statue <note>original: ἀγάλματος; statues in dreams often represented historical figures, saints, or frozen authority</note> a wide space of grain and conversation with justice, he shall depart from a trial, and his passing shall be with goodwill because of his conversation with everyone.

If he sees that he is digging the same earth for someone and reaches the bottom, he shall profit from a lawsuit exactly as much as appeared from the excavated soil. If he sees in that same earth that a pit exists near him and it is dark, he shall be undone and die. But if he sees that the pit is not dark but is surrounded by light, he shall be distressed, but he shall not die; indeed, he shall even recover. Likewise, even in the case of a pit that is simply not wide, or a fall, it is distinguished by fire or fear, and affliction proportional to the pit.

If one believes he is digging a **well** on his own land, if he does not find water, the sun not seeing it, he shall be in want and afflicted. But if he finds pure water, or if no one stopped him, he shall find treasure proportional to the water; and also a child shall inherit his estate. But if the well belongs to a stranger—

If he provides water for others to enter, it signifies his fruitfulness and benefit; likewise, his worldly affairs shall increase and he shall be raised up in wealth. And it shall not only produce for him, but he shall increase his own wealth for himself; his wealth shall be a friend to those in need, and his riches shall be a benefit to many others. If someone sees the **tower** of that same benefactor becoming larger and more spacious, his wealth shall be seen to reach a limit, judged unto the joy and wealth of the world. But if he sees something of the tower or of the **holy things**, it shall be a judgment toward a fortune of abundance. Likewise, for every household, it shall turn out toward timely wealth. If anyone perceives that the **doors** of his house and his gateway were opened, it signifies exile from the world and the departure of his fortune, or it suggests some downfall; and if the value of the doors and gates did not stand firm, they are judged here as being rich, yet it is judged as the destruction of his lineage.

If he sees a downfall, it is as his own destruction, and the destruction of the houses outside his tower, and by the judgment of the one carrying it. If anyone sees the **earth speak** and converse with him, as great as the wonder of the earth speaking is, so much should he wonder at the staves <note>original: ῥαβδοις (rabdois); these rods likely symbolize positions of authority or judicial office.</note> coming upon him from wealth. If a **king** sees this, he shall be long-lived; and with wonder, without war, he shall subdue his enemies and inherit the land of the enemies. But if someone sees that he did not obtain a matter of righteousness, this very joy and strength shall depart from him. But if they see more of a careless voyage, he shall change within those same judgments; it signifies fear of God <note>original: θῦ (theou); a common Byzantine abbreviation for 'God'.</note> and a record of his wicked deeds. If he brings a body, there is more grief than strength, yet joy and glory for his fortune and body...

...shall decrease. If anyone sees white, smooth, and **broad shoulders**, he is strong and humble, where he shall be lamented as if from weakness. The same applies to the **hill** and the surroundings of the hill; those being tested on his high mountains signify, "Lord over the high place and its possessions," or it shall follow a high-ranking man. And he shall understand both fear and obedience in all things, to such a degree as he approached the hill. If he sees it is laid upon him to **tame a deer**, and it is heavy: that which he hates of his fruitfulness shall be taken by his enemy, and he himself shall fall into their own fortunes. For a friend of the common people, he shall become poor and fortune shall depart. If he sees that the shoulders move, it appeared as good fortune, yet because of the maliciousness to be benefited, he shall be in want. If he sees the **forearm** <note>original: πήχυν (pēchyn); literally a cubit or the arm, often representing one's strength or a close companion.</note> because of some known child, for it is because of an exile; let him know fear. For a friend of the common people, his wealth and his work shall be doubled. <insert>+</insert> If anyone sees <unclear>themselves</unclear> in their sleep and there a beautiful **drone** <note>original: κηφὸν (kephon); drones often represent people who live off others, but in a positive dream, they can symbolize a busy, productive household.</note>, they will find expected care and wealth. But if they found a drone of poor wealth, it contains a portion of hatred; it provides a pretext for hatred.

If someone sees a **ship**, they will find a queen. But if they see a ship of all the craftsmen, they will not succeed in their own plan, but will rather be harmed by their favor.

If someone sees that they are digging their own land and they wound it from a height, they will receive wealth and benefit according to that height, having received their fortune.

If someone sees that they hold an **emerald** or a **lychnis** <note>original: λυχνίτην (lychniten); a precious glowing gemstone, often a ruby or garnet, believed in antiquity to shine in the dark.</note> and it illuminates the house and the fortune: if it is a queen, she will rule over a stream or wealth far from every gate.

If one sees that they held a **hawk** under that same earth, it is a sign of fortunes; they will rule and cast him down as if through his ship. Because of the hawk’s sharpness, they did not believe in fear during hunts. If by chance it happened that they saw their own season through which it perishes and burns up by their spirit, they shall not have wealth.

If someone sees that they dug a **well** in the earth and found a garden or a green garden, they will find a beautiful wife, a nation, a child, and a beautiful possession, because of the purity of the water—but also wealth and the enjoyment of grace.

If someone sees that they found a **horse**, or their own horse: if he is a king, he will fear the land or act out of necessity; it shall be called "fear." And the beauty of the houses—fear of his own time—shall be added to the wife and to his wealth.

If someone sees that they built a region or a structure, it will be built for them, but it also signifies force and necessities, because of the increase over others. If someone sees that they sowed a multitude of hidden things, wealth will one day be a grace; and the same for those in the surrounding area because of the hail.

If someone sees that the **earth supported them**: if he is a king, he will receive a great and long-lasting joy. For others, it signifies a foreign conversation with the earth; whoever has not spoken to him, each will progress

or by his own spirit. If someone sees that **fire from heaven** came to him while he was farming or to his place, it signifies the destruction of lofty things and of wealth, but also a very great message, having mastered his hopes. For a king, his greatest and most fearful enemy shall be captured in war.

<margin>AL</margin> If someone sees that the fire of their house entered through the gate which they did not see, it signifies their own counsel, or their death, or they will lose their own people. But if only one of their hands is lost <note>This likely refers to losing a "right-hand" person or a specific servant.</note>.

This is seen from a tower or from the greatest height. Someone saw in a dream: standing before the greatest parts of a monument, having descended, he said to the **dream interpreter** <term>Oneirokrites: a professional diviner who interpreted the symbols of dreams for a fee.</term> who was lying there: "For I saw that a fertile and smooth plain embraced me, I who was honored at the tomb; there was a fig tree and many hands with the ranks, raised up into a hall." And the dream interpreter answered: "The earth of the burial place shaped for its own end signifies your own possessions." And so we are well. Thus the possession of the bystander turned out, though he fell from his own station. And he said to the being:

<margin>to</margin> If the **earthquake** <note>original: σεισμός (seismos); earthquakes in dreams often signify social upheaval or personal instability.</note> is partial, the dream is also partial. If something falls from the house of a person who is suffering, it is thus ordained from the foundation of the Lord that it is in his house. If the **central pillar of the roof** <note>original: κίονας τοῦ μέσου στέγης; the central pillar represents the "pillar of the family," usually the father or master.</note> falls, the death of the master will be announced; it will not cease, with the collapse of the rest of the house, it is a <unclear>disruption</unclear>, that is, a battle with enemies. Furthermore, the falling of the **door** signifies the <margin>to</margin> fall of acquaintances and heads of households. And **fire** upon these things consumes the masters of the house or their fortune, or the head of the household. If something falls from the **molding** <note>original: πλαστοῦ (plastou); refers to decorative plasterwork or stucco.</note> or the structure, the outcome reveals the public face of the result. If it is sluggish toward the length of wealth, it is a glory that will flow toward the death of neighbors. If a **king** himself sees something fall from his own property or his palace, it is judged as his own death or that of those mentioned. It also signifies **war** for the nation, and fear, or a plot against him, and the revelation of his enemies. If a king or a commoner sees that his **house has been widened**, he will perhaps die <note>In ancient dream manuals, a house becoming "too wide" often symbolized the spaciousness of the grave.</note>. If he is a commoner and it is not in the middle of the city, it will be for the sake of fear. But if the fall is at the front—if it is done secretly by a tyrant or even if their path and the palaces are not hidden—the fall is from his own household because of fear of an enemy. If everything falls due to an earthquake and the place becomes a level, great **mountain**, there will be glory and profit for all from him. For the whole does not judge just one person. But the mountain represents high-ranking and **wealthy men**, in proportion to the mountain. If it pertains to all, the suffering and the destruction will be well-known, either through **famine** or through the wrath upon all the wealthy; it is a fear that is unbearable, leading to the seats and joy of the king from the coincidence of the <unclear>events</unclear>. If someone sees a house or a familiar home looking better than before, and those living in it are known, it is a sign of their fortune's end. For that talkative man is the same as the master of the house; it is a world and it is visible. Those who see it widened—

<column-break/>

—quickly. On the same matter, regarding the roof or the master of the house, it brings nothing but <margin>AL</margin> thought or glory, and concern for those dwelling there. And just as the whole—if there are **builders** and the molding, and the space is a familiar area—it signifies the beauty, joy, and **wealth** of the house, in proportion to the construction and the skill of the commoners. If the structure is made of **clay, brick, and wood**, he will find both wealth and joy in proportion to the amount. If it is seen to be of **marble or stone**, he will be long-lived and his wealth will be made invincible. If the structure is made of **iron or bronze**, he will likewise find joy and wealth, but through **struggle** <note>original: μάχης (maches); literally "battle." Metals like iron were associated with the hard work of the forge and the violence of weaponry.</note>, because of the roughness and the fire which is the nature of those materials. Consider how things are made in relation to the light. If the benefit of my house is before my eyes, or below the house toward the earth, it does not concern any of the craftsmen or masters; it holds <term>Hades</term> <note>the underworld or death</note> and a tyrant. If the **wall** falls, or the **roof**, or a part from each side of my house, it means either a nation or wars and the **army** being led away, for it will come to you quickly. Because the door of the house there fell, and from the benefit of the house and its strength, or its falling outward, it will happen to you; it will be joined, or the hairs will be from the west. And just as the judgment is that it will turn white, so shall it turn out. If someone sees a second thing in his house, or nothing better than the others, or an excellence of grace or something greater, it means some rich benefit, or joy and health. If they are from the worst of the grace, departing into hope, it will exist through joy and knowledge. If a stranger ever dwells there, on the road where he is going, that is the place from which these things are judged. And after a certain time, another world. If someone sees that his dwellings were **widened and enlarged** and more than everything, or greater, he will find joy and prevail more than what he possessed. If it is of the people, each will increase in his own **profession**. If it is in the understanding of poverty, or the <unclear>measure</unclear> of how great he is, or a cause and a branch.

...joy less than his hope. If someone, while conversing with [a holy figure], remembers the conversation insatiably, these things for the most part either reach fulfillment or act as a sign that these figures, who are lying near him, were rejoicing with those he spoke with. To the extent that the wonder of the conversation and the appearance is for his own people, and thus after the wonder all the folds of the forms—whatever **images** someone uses in a **dream** <note>original: ὄναρ (onar)</note> regarding battles and the release from them—if it concerns **gold**, the outcome is more favorable. For regarding **silver** items, they are quite blameless but signify **affliction** <note>original: θλίψιν (thlipsin); often used for pressure or distress</note>, because of their nature.

If someone sees **seasonal fruits** <note>original: ὀπώρας (oporas); specifically late summer/autumn fruits</note> that are beautiful in their proper time, his hope is genuine regarding the honor and the luxury associated with them. For there is something [specific] in the craft, and especially a **pattern** <note>original: τύπος (typos)</note> in the Lord, for he will attain the whole spirit of these things. From [the interpretation], he will give certain accounts; likewise his parents [will]. In each of their works, say there is a certain removal of punishment.

The **planting of plants** <note>original: ἵδρυσις φυτῶν (idrysis phyton)</note> is interpreted as being of the same nature as one's own [kin]. First, the folds [of the dream] are again before all those in the **natural judgment** <note>original: φυσικῇ κρίσει (physike krisei)</note>, for the nature of fruits is multifaceted. The **leaves of the trees** are judged according to the **disposition** <note>original: διάθεσιν (diathesin)</note> of the fields. For those that are flourishing and well-clustered immediately signal the state of the **mind** <note>original: γνώμης (gnomes); also means intent or opinion</note>. But those that are weak, sickly, and withered distinguish <margin>se:</margin> minds that are weak toward the task at hand and even evil. ### And fire is distinguished into many "fallings" <note>The word "fallings" (ptomata) here refers to the various outcomes or specific categories of dream events.</note>.

If someone sees that someone is burning the gate of his house or tower with a bright flame, the master of the house or the tower will perish in a common way, either by the struggle of enemies or disease. If he sees fire without a flame, and not everything is burning, but it burns in other parts, it foretells their suffering. If someone sees an "official fire," <note>original: πῦρ ἀρχοντικὸν; fire associated with the ruling class or government.</note> his suffering will be judged according to the state and the city. If someone sees that they burned something because of sin, it leads to suffering and the destruction of the persons we previously mentioned; each is judged according to the person. Likewise, if someone sees that one of his limbs was burned, the suffering will be in that specific part, with the limbs being pre-judged. If someone sees glowing coals of fire without smoke or flame, he will gain **orphan's gold** <note>original: χριστὸν ὀρφανικὸν (christon orphanikon); likely a corruption of "chryson," referring to unexpected wealth or an inheritance from a estate without heirs.</note>, proportional to the duration of the fire. If he sees a burning flame that does not consume, he will first be held responsible for evils and the consumption of the burning. If he was burned by the flame, he will be punished by a "discharge" <note>possibly a legal penalty or a physical ailment.</note>. Thus, if the eyes of the family or the children [are seen], or if fire is lit with wood, it suggests a battle or a verbal argument with them. If someone sees that they are warming bread or food in the fire to eat, these things will lead to health and prosperity, though through various fears and trembling. <meta>This page continues the manual of dream interpretation, moving from the general symbolism of the sea (the Emperor) to the specific symbolism of ships and naval vessels. In the Byzantine world, the navy was the backbone of imperial power, so dreams about ships often related to one's livelihood, family, or the state of the empire itself.</meta>

...a ship. If someone sees that they are trading by using the oars of a ship, they will amass silver from their possessions and will see a great profit. If someone sees that their baggage was taken away from them, then their own will and purpose have been brought to an end. 

If we see that ships have departed from the midst of an approaching vessel, or if someone sees that they have cabbages <note>original: κράμβας; in ancient dream-lore, cabbages often symbolized sorrow, labor, or a "heavy head"</note> in their rowing-space, they shall find long-lasting worries. If they see a long table, the results are the same. These same interpretations apply to new ships as well. 

If someone sees a ship leaping out of the sea, or that its prow <note>original: στόμα; literally "mouth"</note> is fearsomely on fire, and the ship is unable to catch the wind, that person will suffer a loss in their faith and will go into mourning. But if the ship remains upright, it shows that each person will remain in their state of delight. 

If someone sees a slave belonging to some merchant upon a ship, the interpretation is according to what is found in that household. And if someone sees that they drank water from the ship’s bilge <note>original: διευσμάτων; referring to the leakage or collected water in the hull</note>, such a dream indicates they will be enslaved and fall into poverty. 

If someone sees an addition made to a ship by means of pack-animals <note>original: ἀλόγων; literally "unreasoning creatures"</note> for the success of the imperial fleet: 

**The imperial ships used for war** represent a lion and terror. And the transport ships <note>original: πλοῖα τὰ ὑποζύγια; ships used for carrying animals or heavy cargo</note> represent a household and its affairs. Proclamations about them are interpreted similarly. These ships, when seen in the same context, are judged according to the person of the King. 

**If someone sees that the imperial dromon <term>dromon</term> <note>original: δρόμων; the standard war galley of the Byzantine navy, powered by oars and sails</note> was split** or destroyed, there will be a loss for the shipwright. If someone sees that their dromon has ceased its movement, they will fall ill in a manner proportional to the ship's affliction. If someone sees it in relation to their own seat, they shall die and their affairs with them. 

If someone sees that they have built a dromon, they will find a wife proportional to its abundance and beauty. If someone sees that the dromon is standing still within that same ship, they will find through her a son and an heir for their burial. If someone sees that the dromon was broken, even if it is wide or suffering, it is judged as the loss of his son. 

If someone sees that their dromon was forbidden from the sea, they themselves will enter into tribulation and confusion, proportional to the aforementioned swarm <note>original: ἐσμοῦ; perhaps referring to a crowd or a swarm of troubles</note>, though they shall not perish.

This also applies to the winds. 

If someone sees that their ship has a great number of oars and the equipment for war and is sailing well, their power will be established in proportion to the oars and the ship. If someone sees that their gifts became slabs and metals, they will find even more, for they will find one thing strong and another alongside it. 

If someone sees that the ships are launching fire <note>original: πέμπουσι πῦρ; likely a reference to "Greek Fire," the incendiary weapon used by the Byzantine navy</note>, it refers to the arrival of the first ships; one recognizes the enemies by how much the fire destroys.

If someone sees a ship, they will find tribulation and disease from it. <margin>147</margin> If the vantage point <note>original: σκοπιά; often referring to a lookout or a specific perspective within the dream</note> comes from the same water, the suffering will be longer-lasting. But if the vantage point is by chance and then ceases, everyone will experience the suffering. Regarding the heating of water: this refers to the water itself.
<margin>148</margin> If someone sees that they drank hot water, they shall find joy and a measure of pourable liquid, in proportion to "the 77" <note>original: τῆς ζζ'; likely a reference to a specific numbered section or category in the dream-manual's index</note>. For as much as the chance judgment leads to good, so much does the boiling water lead to the same. If it falls under affliction, they shall find affliction upon it. But if they drank wine and it was hot, they shall find power. If they see that they drink for their benefit, they shall find affliction from their own relatives. If they see that they suffer from heat in their body, they shall find joy and delight in their family. If their spirit <note>original: πνεῦμα; can mean breath or life-force</note> drinks heat, or if their face does, this will also be for others according to "the 77."

<margin>149</margin> **Concerning the Bathhouse:** Speaking from this: you wish to be nourished, and you shall walk toward what is good. If there comes a sense of greed or the bitter joy of life, it shall be for the sake of piety, or something else arising from spiritual fervor.
<margin>150</margin> If one sees themselves washing with excellent water or finishing their wash, and if this leads to joy, it is especially concerning other pleasures. If someone sees that they were caught in adultery in a bathhouse and yet they find justice and wealth—or rather, if they are already rich—this is beneficial regarding their efforts <note>original: πέρσαις; likely a corruption of "deeds" or "endeavors"</note>. It is a good sign to be cleansed of the grime of the hair. If someone sees a high house or room in the heat, they shall find lesser affliction and worry. If water is offered to them, it is a greater sign of joy and follows from what is to come. If the bath is sorrowful, it represents the moderation of the bathhouse.
<margin>151</margin> Concerning the finding of scents and that which comes from the revelation of health: if someone sees that they find vegetable-water <note>original: ὑδάτιον λαχάνων</note> prepared in their house, their gold is prepared fortunately and without failure, or 
<margin>152</margin> they shall guard what is most precious. Great glory shall be kept for them by men. Grace shall be revealed in them as before. But if they see that they lost that very water, they shall come to loss and harm; this is a foundational judgment. The poor man, however, shall be judged toward wealth and the prime of life. If someone sees that their spirit leaped into

<column-break/>

a glass vessel <note>original: ὑελίγον; a common symbol for fragility or the womb in dream-lore</note> of water, they shall find a wife and the bodies of children for all.
<margin>153</margin> It produces the causes within the body. And it does not show that bitterness remains hidden. And in the "water of the Scythians," there they shall die, but the one born shall live.
<margin>154</margin> If someone sees that they found hot water and threw it away, a daughter <note>original: θυγέραται; variant of θυγάτηρ</note> shall be born, but not quickly. If they see that a better glass vessel was found, there shall be help for the child even after they have toiled. And fame, or strange things, shall be seen in the bathhouse.
<margin>155</margin> If someone sees that they have water and it was taken from them, it leads to fame and glory.
<margin>156</margin> If someone sees that water is poured out, very pure water, and they took it from a spring, let them look to their worries, for the spiritual ones dwell there. And what they sought, they shall be enriched by. They shall live, not by what is spoken, but height and mortals shall be established. The judgments of the people shall be hers. If they are found as a youth, or as a commoner, so shall the day be. But if they were "slain" in the bathhouse <note>original: ἐσφάγη; likely a metaphor for a deep spiritual or physical cleansing</note>, they shall find a succession from the walking of the noble, and shall be judged healthy.
<margin>157</margin> If the "flock" <note>original: ἀγέλη; could refer to a crowd or a specific vessel</note> broke before their own water, they shall find worry and affliction shall come to their fortunes. But if they see that they broke it with their own hand, they shall find affliction in the breaking. But if they see that they saved the dirt of their house, and they hold that specific dirt, their life shall be in balance, more than the world’s, and they shall help others. If they drink from glass but do not hold it in the judgment, they shall lose these things. Similarly, if they cleaned drachmas <note>original: δραχμὰς; silver coins</note> of the house, they shall be practical in these evidences. But if they see that their spirit makes things and a bridle for their testimony, they shall find harm, or 
<margin>158</margin> lose the drachma. If they see that they moved around their house, and the judgment is white and bright, they shall find joy in proportion to the whiteness. But if the judgment is common and black, they shall find worry and a multitude of bitter things. If they see they found it only in dry and discarded places, they shall find a daily taking of accounts and labor, in proportion. If they see a multitude of bricks: if they are poor, they shall rather grow rich; but if they are rich, he lifts up his wealth and secures it.

If anyone sees his **mill** <note>original: μύλωνα; the mill was a central symbol of household economy and daily bread in the Byzantine world</note> being built, he shall find goodness and good fortune in his works. If he sees that a woman finds the mill, it signifies an abundance of nature through good wheat. ### On the Majesty of the King and the Fate of Houses

...or even more beautiful. She will find joy in her husband and in her fortune. But if she sees that she has lost her veil <note>original: μαφερειον (maphorion) — a traditional Byzantine woman’s head-covering or shawl</note>, she will find affliction and separation from her husband or her fortune. If she sees that she is wearing a black veil and loses it, this signifies wealth again and great good fortune. If she sees that this garment is clean, then she herself is clean. But if she sees that all her clothes are like this, or something old, or a veil or something else belonging to someone else, such things happen to the woman. If a married woman sees that she is washing—that is, the things of the woman and the bath. But if she sees that she walked half-uncovered <note>original: ασκεπη (askepe) — without a head-covering, which was a sign of shame for women in Byzantine society</note>, or the other part [was uncovered]. If she sees that men or a woman suffer, it means they will put an end to the evil and the turmoil. And just as he said, so it happened: and his wife died.

### Concerning women’s hair. From the Persians and the Egyptians:

<margin>104a</margin>
If a woman sees that she is cutting the hair of her head, her husband will die <insert>or die</insert> or she will be separated from him. If she sees that she is shearing her head, by her own power and that of her husband, a separation is being prepared by her. If she sees that she has turned the hair of her head and [pulled] it back again, this signifies a jealous person who will take her husband into her separation. If she sees that she holds her hair and cuts into it, it signifies afflictions and her separation from him. Or if the woman herself does the shearing. <unclear>earē</unclear> or that his wife has been sheared—her face. And she will find affliction and separation from that husband. Just as if she were found again or if she sheared herself, and he is the one washing her. And she is judged to be separated from her husband. For all things, whether by appearance or that she provides her own shearing. If a woman sees her [hair], and it is not there, she will lose her husband. Or the shears(?)

<margin>104e</margin>
If she sees that she wears the clothes of ancient women, she will find passion and love for her sun <note>original: ηλου (ēlou) — possibly a misspelling of 'ηλιου' (heliou - sun), or referring to a 'nail/stud', but likely 'husband' or 'glory' in context</note>, and fear of God. But also good fortune, for it is proportional. If a poor woman sees herself wearing such things, she will find a lord. But it is a passion if it is lost to her. If she sees how great is the [clothing] of men and of a rich man.

...she will find humiliation and shame for his wife. If he sees that his wife came and wore another’s [clothing], there is affliction for her and public talk of women. Behind <unclear>aphor</unclear> them. It shall lead to her glory, and it is judged as frugality. If he sees that his wife wore beautiful things, yet old ones appear somewhere, and the husband as well; if she saw old things through her, she will find evil, and in the affliction(?). If she sees that she wore a breastplate <note>original: θωρακιον (thorakion) — a small breastplate or a decorative stiffened garment</note>, she is judged among men. And it signifies an inheritance of the woman from the husband. If she sees that she wore the tunic and shoes of a man, and the children, it leads to childbearing and success. But those who are deceitful judge [otherwise]. If she sees that she wore artificial weapons of war, she will find authority over her husband, and fearlessness toward enemies—that is, her fortune, or someone regarding the management of her house. And if she sees the weapons in the [house?], she will find her sin <note>perhaps 'atonement' or 'end of sin' in context</note>, wealth, and long life. If it were from <unclear>zamos</unclear> of the Lord, she will find wealth and afflictions. And a thief of an inheritance(?)

### From the Persians and Egyptians: Concerning all things, it is judged by the person.

<margin>105</margin>
If someone sees that they hold the weapons of the kingdom—that is, the weapons of peace—they will fight for authority over enemies. Either for the kingdom and for the women, and it is pleasing for victory over the enemy. If a leader of the world's people sees this, he will release the honor of the slave upon an uprising or tyranny against him, or against himself, the weapons of old; in the drinking, may he not find it, or seeing it for fortune. He shall reign. The woman will find great glory. If she was being insulted, she will find humiliation. If one sees a king, he shall enslave an enemy kingdom. If he saw an arrow or heard of wars or other such things, he will find fear and trembling regarding authority. For all things regarding the release of the change, if one sees that someone has come from his presence and turned to flight: if he is a king, he shall conquer him alone; if he is a tyrant, he holds the kingdom. These symbols are frequently linked to the Emperor (the King) and the acquisition of wealth or the presence of enemies. ...he will find some good from the king, as well as wealth and glory, and triumph over every enemy of his. If someone sees that he had an old ship <note>original: πλοῖον (ploion) — in dream interpretation, ships often symbolize the support structure of one's life or a journey toward wealth</note>, he will find wealth amidst fear and sweetness. If he sees that a warship is consuming something, it will reveal things concerning his mother or the king's authority. If a woman sees this, she will find gold or drachmas <note>original: δραχμάς — a unit of currency</note> and partial wealth. If a woman finds an enemy's ship. If someone sees a lion <note>original: λέων (leon)</note> with arrows and it was light, he will find wealth that is easily gained. 

If someone sees that he found a royal trireme <note>original: τριήριον — a galley with three banks of oars, representing the pinnacle of state naval power</note>; if a woman sees the part of other ships, a king or a rich man will find gold. Regarding the common people, such a dream means they will find wealth and hope from the sea. If someone in their sleep finds a lion’s skin, it signifies the greatest wealth or the highest honor from the king, which will come very quickly. If someone who is a king sees a cowl <note>original: κουκουλιου (koukouliou) — a monastic or protective hood</note> lying there, or if he sees he is among pleasurable leaders, he will become rich immediately. If a woman sees a lion offering her a gift, she should fear a great enemy in the near future. If he sees that his ship was being carried away, it shows that allies have arrived. 

If he sees that the king, for the sake of his children and very good deeds, comes to their defense, and if grapevines <note>original: ἡμερίδαι (hemeridai)</note> or the affairs of the kingdom are overturned, these things are interpreted as coming from joy and the permanence of children. If a poor man sees the king malnourished, it signifies war with his own enemies. If he sees that someone conversed with charms and pleasures within a ship, the wonder of that conversation signifies the desolation of the kingdom.

### Concerning elephants: from the Indian books:

The elephant is interpreted as a king or a powerful, wealthy man. It is not only judged in relation to a great enemy, but its proportions are also measured. If someone sees that he discovered an elephant, he has found wealth or immense, untold riches; these are also the laws of the king, as they are prescribed. If someone saw himself in the king’s chariot... he saw that when he sold the elephant, he gained authority from its value, and his testimony will be of great importance. If someone sees that an elephant died...

<column-break/>

...his own, he should expect the desired thing he hoped for but not receive it. Wealth comes with strife; the wealth of elephants belongs to the rulers. If someone sees that he found a piece of an elephant <note>likely a reference to ivory</note>, he will find wealth through a middleman and great riches. If he sees the wealth of an elephant, it signifies partial wealth or money corresponding to the number of his soldiers, based on the faces and the ships themselves. 

The elephant hints at a man of high rank <note>original: ὕπαρχον (hyparchon) — a prefect or high official</note> who is close to authority and great wealth, because it is hunted everywhere for its nobility. If the king sees that he acquired an elephant from the outside, it signifies great wealth, men, and weapons of war for security. If a man sees himself standing or being embittered [by an elephant], he will suffer a great insult from a ruler. 

If he sees that he orders his beard <note>original: πώγων (pogon)</note> to be struck near [the beast], such a man will kill and take command of his wealth and will cause him distress. If he sees that he carries the elephant on his back, he will be granted great honor. If someone else sees that the elephant met with misfortune, it signifies a lack, though joy and wealth will be less intense. If he sees that he fell from an elephant or is questioned about wealth, he will serve a very great man, gaining authority and profit for himself. If the elephant suddenly enters his house as a stranger, he will find joy and improvement from the king. If he finds its bones or its dung <note>original: κόπρου (koprou)</note>, this is interpreted as a sign of wealth.

The leopard <note>original: πάρδος (pardos) — often represents a bold, treacherous, or boastful enemy</note> is judged as a boastful enemy. If someone sees that he went away from old leopards, he will find war accompanied by turmoil, deceit, and fear. If he sees that he cherished the beast, he will speak his mind. If he sees that he killed it, he will strike down such an enemy. If a poor man from the common people sees it, he will find punishment and fear from a man in authority. If he sees that he is bitten by the leopard, he will receive great punishment from an official. If he washes the leopard...

...of a sorcerer <note>original: φαρμακοῦ (pharmakou) — can mean a poisoner or a practitioner of dark magic</note>. If anyone sees the carcass of a horned beast or a panther <note>original: πίνδου (pindou) — likely a scribal error for πάρδου (pardou), meaning leopard or panther</note>, he will find wealth and glory. If he dreams that a panther was captured, if he is a poor stranger or a king, it signifies a powerful enemy greater than himself. If the beast has curly hair, he will attain greater glory and will become prideful. <margin>195</margin> If he sees that a panther is given as a gift, or he gives one to someone, he will humble a beloved enemy, or he will receive a gift from an unexpected source. If he eats its meat—that of a panther—he will find glory and great honor, and the submission of a faithful man.

->Concerning the wolf and the panther; from the Persians and Egyptians:<-

<margin>196</margin> The wolf and the panther: if he finds an enemy and is with him, it will go badly for him afterward. Because of this, if you see yourself falling into traps, behold, expect death. And this refers to his servant. If someone sees that he is fighting with a wolf, he will conquer with authority and will be victorious. Learn that he will find wealth from his enemy, or perhaps war; the dream again concerns evils. It also happens that if someone sees the panther and a woman, it means a poor woman; he will find fear and punishment from
<margin>197</margin> some authority and temptation from the poor. The bear <note>original: ἄρκτος (arktos)</note> represents a rich and powerful enemy. And concerning judgment: if someone sees that a bear overpowered him, he will slay his own enemy, and he who journeys will be robbed. If he sees that he is drinking its milk, he will find great authority. If he sees that he eats its multitudes <note>likely meaning its young or its flesh in abundance</note>, he will prevail over his enemy through famine. If he sees that he ate its meat, he will find wealth through an obscure word and the power of riches. If he sees a male bear, it represents his father, who treats the enemy's flesh as meat. If he sees that he drinks its milk, he will find fear from authority and reproach. If he sees that he holds its head or tastes it, he will find a rich portion of the enemy; he encompasses the head
<margin>198</margin> of that one's wealth. From the Indians: The hyena-fly <note>original: μυῖαγα — a likely corruption or hybrid term for the hyena, as the text immediately transitions to hyena imagery</note> fights against the body of some mistress who is a sorceress or a girl's stylist; and it is moderate. If someone sees that he goes and sells it, he [saves] a woman and saves everyone.

<column-break/>

If he sees that he eats the meat of a hyena <note>original: ὑαίνης (hyaines)</note>, he is being bewitched by that same woman or is attempting to dance with strange things. If he sees that he threw a spear or a stone at it, he shall send nothing to her and evil talk will be made. If he sees that she again gives him something to eat, it is because such a woman is preserving his status. If he sees that he drinks the milk of a hyena, he will find a loss leading to poverty.

<margin>199</margin> The Fox: From the Persians: The wolf is judged as the persona of a greedy and disorderly man. If he persuades the wolf or fights it, he will find authority and war from some ruler. If he sees that he conquered it and has authority, it signifies the entry of an enemy who has lost everything. If he sees that he is wandering—if he sees the wanderings of a wolf—he will find punishment and love from his enemy and a greedy man. He shall eat [the meat], for he has a will toward him. To them, wolves also make enemies out of conviction. In these same matters, he will also destroy her; someone may be persuaded through words. If he sees that he sent [messengers] against them like poor men, he will fight his enemy and those of foreign tribes. And according to the effect of the meat, so shall be the honor. If he sees that he is a lily <note>original: κρῖνος — likely a corruption of a verb for 'judging' or 'choosing'</note> or drinks wolf's milk, he will receive honor, but he will also possess the anger of some enemy. The Fox: from the Indians and Egyptians:

<margin>200</margin> The fox, in that it fights defensively, represents a battle with one's own versatile and evil [nature]; because they make him their hope, he will find affliction from his own... and [deceptive] gains through words of wandering. If he sees that he ate a silent one <note>perhaps a reference to a specific type of fox or a quiet enemy</note>, he will abandon it. If he sees that he hides a stolen fox, he will find a refuge with an evil woman. If he sees her looking around at him, he will find a plot from her. If he sees that he plays with a fox, or eats its meat, he will find the friendship of a woman and honor, and he will have a portion with her. If he sees that he drinks fox milk, having suffered a sickness of mine, he recovers. If he... <note>unclear verb</note>, he will be rid of her.
